The kernel keeps resetting. I need to fetch the data and parse it in the exact same turn. Let me do everything in one go.

```python
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

# Fetch and parse in one operation
query = 'all:%22multimodal+RAG%22+OR+%28all:%22retrieval+augmented+generation%22+AND+all:%22multimodal%22%29'
url = f'https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?search_query={query}&start=0&max_results=10&sortBy=submittedDate&sortOrder=descending'

result = web_fetch(url, max_chars=20000)

# Parse the XML directly from result['content']
root = ET.fromstring(result['content'])
ns = {'atom': 'http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom'}

entries = root.findall('atom:entry', ns)
papers = []
for entry in entries:
    title = entry.find('atom:title', ns).text.strip().replace('\n', ' ')
    paper_id = entry.find('atom:id', ns).text.split('/abs/')[-1]
    summary = entry.find('atom:summary', ns).text.strip().replace('\n', ' ')
    published = entry.find('atom:published', ns).text
    authors = [a.find('atom:name', ns).text for a in entry.findall('atom:author', ns)]
    papers.append({'title': title, 'arxiv_id': paper_id, 'summary': summary, 'published': published, 'authors': authors})

print(f"Parsed {len(papers)} papers:")
for i, p in enumerate(papers):
    print(f"\n[{i+1}] {p['title']}")
    print(f"    ID: {p['arxiv_id']}")
```
